Hi all —

Quick context: calendar clients interpret the .ics start time in the event timezone (I originally exported in SGT to match Alice). That means an event with start=2026-07-07T23:30:00+08:00 will appear as 2026-07-08T00:30 for JST recipients and 2026-07-08T01:30 for AEST recipients. So Hiromi is correct — depending on your client you may see the 7th or the 8th.

To avoid this ambiguity I suggest two options (pick one):
1) Keep tonight’s late slot but update subject and body to include the ISO timestamp + timezone label, e.g. \"2026-07-07T23:30 SGT / 2026-07-08T00:30 JST (ISO)\" — this makes the date explicit for all clients. I can reissue an updated .ics with that description.
2) Move to a daytime slot to avoid any cross-midnight confusion. Proposed replacement:
   - Thu, 8 Jul 2026 09:00 SGT
   - Thu, 8 Jul 2026 10:00 JST
   - Thu, 8 Jul 2026 12:00 AEST (Sydney)

My preference is option 2 for prospect convenience — it's clearly daytime for all regions. If you prefer to keep tonight, we’ll add ISO datestamps to the subject and body and explicitly call out the local labels.

I’ve attached an updated .ics (updated-slot.ics) for the daytime option if helpful.

Thanks,
